newsitem.title: USA: American Eagle silver coin sales jump in November.
newsitem.headline: American Eagle silver coin sales jump in November.

text.p: Sales of American Eagle silver coins rose in November as silver prices fell, but sales of American Eagle gold coins did not change much as gold prices fell, industry consultants CPM Group said.
Silver coin sales rose to 485,000 ounces in November, almost twice as much as the 250,000 ounces sold in October.
"This was a steady continuation of the 95.2 pct increase in sales last month," CPM Group managing director Jeffrey Christian said.
In recent months, the average price of silver has steadily fallen from $5.05 an ounce in September to $4.94 in October and to $4.83 in November.
Measured year-on-year, silver coin sales posted a 56.5 pct gain over the 310,000 ounces sold in November 1995.
American Eagle gold coin sales saw only modest gains, rising 4.8 pct to 22,000 ounces against 21,000 ounces in October.
As the average price of gold did not fluctuate as much as silver, sales remained constant, CPM Group said.
Gold coin sales dropped 18.5 pct from 27,000 ounces in November last year.
The premiums for the most popular silver coins rose in November, while the premiums for platinum and gold coins were unchanged.
